public_rationale: The $10 billion contribution was not independently verified. Microsoft's public disclosure establishes an annualized $13 billion revenue threshold, but gives no OpenAI breakdown. The linked report could not be retrieved, and later spending forecasts do not establish that $10 billion belonged within the same $13 billion revenue estimate. The run-rate mismatch warrants caution, not a definitive contradiction of the claimed customer share.
limitations: The central underlying report was inaccessible through read_page.
Company-reported run rate and press-estimated annual revenue are different measures.
No comparable customer-level revenue record was established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: About $10 billion of Microsoft's $13 billion AI revenue comes from OpenAI's Azure compute spend.

statement.excerpt: Also, this is not profit, and $10 billion of that comes from OpenAI’s compute spend on Azure.

from_speaker: projected to make $13 billion in annual revenue this year from AI
our_interpretation: The surrounding paragraph attributes the figures to reporting about 2025 revenue, so assess the claimed composition of that estimate.
The plain reading is that approximately $10 billion of the same $13 billion Microsoft AI revenue total is attributable to OpenAI purchasing Azure compute.
Both figures must use the same period, recognition basis and revenue definition.
The post also invokes Microsoft's January annualized run rate. Do not silently substitute that run rate for the reported full-year estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Accessible reporting or company records establish approximately $10 billion of OpenAI Azure compute revenue within the same approximately $13 billion Microsoft AI revenue estimate for 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different OpenAI compute contribution, or show that the two cited figures cannot form the claimed same-period revenue breakdown.
